plan.estimand: Minimum total sample size for Riley binary development criteria with shrinkage adjustment
plan.hypothesis: Model development study with internal validation; precision requirement on adjusted Cox-Snell R-squared with shrinkage compensation
assumptions: pmsampsize 1.1.3 package with Riley binary development criteria
Default absolute precision criteria applied
Nagelkerke scale for R-squared difference (binary outcome context)
Shrinkage factor of 0.95 applied to anticipated adjusted Cox-Snell R-squared
95% confidence level for precision calculation
Internal validation with apparent versus adjusted performance shrinkage
Maximum absolute difference of 0.05 on Nagelkerke scale is the primary precision constraint
scientific_notes: Riley et al. (2020) binary prediction model development criteria: minimum event and non-event counts to ensure stable predictor estimates and adequate internal validation precision
Cox-Snell R-squared: underlying performance metric before shrinkage adjustment
Adjusted Cox-Snell R-squared: performance after shrinkage, reflecting apparent-to-adjusted shrinkage (internal validation penalty)
Nagelkerke scale: normalized R-squared, often preferred for communication in binary/survival contexts; typical thresholds: 0.05 absolute difference represents clinically meaningful precision
Outcome-risk precision: margin of error on predicted probabilities, additional constraint for individual-level predictions
The user requests verification of outcome-risk precision at the returned sample size (secondary metric)
